requirement: User passwords are encrypted with bcrypt before being stored; passwords are never stored in plaintext.
label: GAP
evidence: register() inserts {"password": password} directly into mongo.db.users; ensure_owner_user() inserts {"password": OWNER_PASSWORD} directly; login() queries mongo.db.users.find_one({"name": name, "password": password}), which relies on plaintext password storage/comparison.
reasoning: There is code handling password storage and authentication, but none of it uses bcrypt or any hashing/encryption step before persistence. The stored password field is the raw input/environment value, and login compares plaintext directly against the database, so a test requiring bcrypt-stored non-plaintext passwords would fail. Per the decision guide, because there is no behavior addressing bcrypt storage at all, this is GAP.
